summary_en: KOBE BUSSAN announced a 60 billion yen euro-denominated convertible bond issuance with a 7-year maturity and 0% coupon, alongside a share buyback program of up to 4 billion yen or 16 million shares from September 30, 2026 to April 30, 2027, with planned execution via ToSTNeT-3 immediately after decision.
title_en: Supplementary Explanation Material Regarding Euro-Denominated Convertible Bond Issuance and Share Buyback
translation_en_brief:
On September 29, 2026, KOBE BUSSAN decided to issue a 60 billion yen euro-denominated convertible bond with a 7-year maturity, zero coupon, and a redemption price at par. The bond carries conversion restrictions, put options after 5 years, and cash settlement acquisition rights. Concurrently, the company authorized a share buyback program with a maximum budget of 4 billion yen and share limit of 16 million shares, representing execution between September 30, 2026 and April 30, 2027.

The company plans to execute the buyback primarily through ToSTNeT-3 (an off-market trading system) immediately following the board decision on September 30, 2026. If the amount acquired via ToSTNeT-3 falls short of the 4 billion yen ceiling, the company intends to continue purchasing shares via market purchases, considering prevailing market conditions and applicable regulations.

The offering includes a 180-day lock-up agreement applicable to the company itself, GYOMU SUPER JAPAN DREAM FOUNDATION, COCCOLARE CO., LTD., Hirokazu Numata, and M&U Asset Management LLC. Morgan Stanley & Co. International plc serves as the active bookrunner. The convertible bond settlement is scheduled for October 15, 2026, with a redemption date of September 30, 2033.
